headline_marked: LG Display unveils [[FLiPP]] OLED tech: 1.6x brighter, 2.4x longer lifespan
headline: LG Display unveils FLiPP OLED tech: 1.6x brighter, 2.4x longer lifespan
summary: LG Display's new FLiPP manufacturing method ditches fine metal masks for photolithography, promising brighter, more efficient, and longer-lasting OLED panels.
details: LG Display has introduced FLiPP (FMM-Less innovative Pixel Patterning), a new OLED manufacturing technique designed to overcome current limitations. This technology aims to create panels that are brighter, more energy-efficient, and have significantly extended lifespans.

Unlike conventional RGB OLEDs that use a fine metal mask (FMM) for pixel patterning, FLiPP employs photolithography and UV light. This method positions RGB pixels in order and then selectively removes unnecessary areas, avoiding the cost and potential alignment issues associated with FMMs, especially on larger panels.
LG Display claims FLiPP panels are 1.6 times brighter and last 2.4 times longer than FMM panels. Additionally, they offer a 13 percent reduction in power consumption.
The FLiPP technology is also said to be free from panel size and resolution constraints, opening possibilities for virtually any display requirement, including VR and AR applications.

Initially, LG Display plans to implement FLiPP in IT applications like tablets and monitors. The company intends to expand its use to larger products such as ultra-large TVs and even small 1-inch wearable devices in the future.
Specific production timelines and the availability of the first products featuring FLiPP technology have not yet been announced.
